description: Pinned identity of the TAXSIM executable used by the axiom-oracles TAXSIM adapter. The adapter shells out to a TAXSIM binary bundled inside the policyengine-taxsim distribution (imported dynamically as TaxsimRunner); the binary itself is not vendored in this repo. This file pins the reproducible provenance of that binary: the exact policyengine-taxsim release, its PyPI sdist/wheel SHA-256 (the source of truth for the bundled binary), and, for each bundled executable extracted from that wheel, its SHA-256, byte size, executable format, NBER build stamp and the law years it accepts. `build` is the quoted stamp embedded in the executable's bytes (pins.read_build_stamp); the macOS and Linux builds print the same stamp as the last column of their CSV output header. `law_years` records what the executable did when it was run: the law years it was given that produced output (`ran`), the ones it refused (`rejected`), the verbatim first line it printed for a refused year (`rejection`), and `first`/`last`, the range that line states. Years between `ran` entries were not run. null means the executable has not been executed. `format` is the description file(1) (file-5.41) printed for the executable, verbatim. Without this pin no oracle number produced against TAXSIM is reproducible (Phase-A item A2). Schema v2 adds `binaries`, every TAXSIM executable the adapter may run keyed by SHA-256 (with its byte size, build stamp, platform and the pinned git, URL or wheel sources its bytes can be fetched from), and named `profiles` that map each (TAXSIM SOI state, law year, platform) to one of those binaries: a profile default plus declarative overrides. The runner resolves every row's binary from the active profile (`default_profile` unless a run names another) and runs only bytes whose SHA-256 and size equal that pin; it never falls back to another executable.

runtime_binary.note: policyengine-taxsim's TaxsimRunner selects the binary by platform.system() from {sys.prefix}/share/policyengine_taxsim/taxsimtest/<name>; axiom-oracles resolves the same file with pins.installed_binary_path() and passes it explicitly. The per-platform executables are different NBER builds (see each bundled_binaries entry). They accept different law years: the Linux build refused 2025-2027 and the macOS build refused only 2027, so of the platform binaries that have been run, only the macOS one accepts law years 2025 and 2026 (the Windows binary has not been run). They also disagree in years both accept: on one single filer with $50,000 of wages (state 0, idtl 0) at 2024 the Linux build returned fiitax 4016.12 and frate 12.00 where the macOS build returned 4016.00 and 0.00, and at 1960 fiitax 25668.00 where the macOS build returned 0.00. A TAXSIM number is therefore specific to the binary that produced it. The callers that run the pinned binary check the requested law years against its pinned range first (pins.require_law_years) and record the identity of the binary they ran (pins.binary_identity). No CI workflow installs the taxsim extra, and every TAXSIM comparison suite is ci: manual, so these binaries run only where a person runs them.

law_years.evidence: Run 2026-10-10 through PolicyEngine/policyengine-taxsim resources/taxsimtest/taxsim-docker-wrapper.sh at 549beade32dbc43cb31d2f37e46bec983660d28d (ubuntu:24.04 + gfortran runtime, linux/amd64, colima on macOS) on one-record inputs. pe-taxsim-main-2026-08.description: The August 18 builds that policyengine-taxsim main bundled (resources/taxsimtest) from PR #1150 until PR #1206 merged on 2026-11-02 and replaced the macOS and Linux builds with the November 1 builds; the policyengine-taxsim 2.31.7 wheel bundles them. Every state and year.

dashboard-2026-09.description: The Linux build the PolicyEngine TAXSIM emulator dashboard ran for its September 2026 refresh (metadata.taxsimBinarySha256 in dashboard/public/data/<year>/summary_<year>.json, 2021-2025, in PolicyEngine/policyengine-taxsim: the September 9 Linux build), and the macOS and Windows builds that pe-taxsim commit c245a3eb bundles with it (the September 9 macOS build and the September 1 Windows build, cd2026090110); the metadata records no macOS or Windows binary. Georgia and Maryland in 2024 and 2025 run the August builds instead: metadata.taxsimFallback records the August Linux build (00a321d2...) for them, because the September Linux build crashes there, and the override's reason pairs it with the matching August macOS and Windows builds.

overrides.reason: metadata.taxsimFallback in the dashboard's summary_2024.json and summary_2025.json records {states: [GA, MD], years: [2024, 2025], sha256: 00a321d2..., sourceCommit: 2b69146b..., reason: 'September Linux TAXSIM SIGFPE in gatax24 and mdtax22; previous binary for complete GA/MD outputs'}; summary_2021.json through summary_2023.json record no fallback. The crash was observed on Linux; the override names the matching August build on every platform so a profile resolves the same vintage per (state, year) on any host.
